title: The empty history panel prints its capture shortcuts backwards
goal: When you open the capture history with nothing in it, the app tells you which keys to press, and it prints those keys in the opposite order from how macOS itself writes them and from how the rest of the design study now writes them. This makes the one shortcut hint the app shows a person match everywhere else.
notes: Found while sweeping the design study for modifier order (keyboard-shortcuts-read-in-one-modifier-order-ac). Sources has 34 occurrences of the cmd-first glyph pair but 33 are code comments; exactly ONE is user-facing: Sources/Photonz/HistoryOverlay.swift:65 emptyMessage("No captures yet. CMD-SHIFT-4 grabs a rectangle, CMD-SHIFT-3 the full screen, CMD-SHIFT-5 records."). Swap to shift-first. HistoryOverlay.swift is shared (not forked into Releases/Next), so one edit reaches both releases, but it does change Current-release copy, which is why the sweep task left it alone. Zero occurrences of the cmd-before-option pair in Sources. The comments are worth normalising in the same pass for grep-ability but are not user-facing. The authoring rule now lives in docs/design/mocks/shared/AGENTS.md under the keyboard-shortcut carve-out, and the study publishes it on pages/lang-keyboard.html section 05.
acceptance: The empty capture history message prints its three shortcuts in the macOS order, shift before command
No user-visible string anywhere in the app prints a command key before a shift or option key
Tests pass and the app builds

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the hint is the only shortcut copy the app shows a person outside the Welcome window, and WelcomeView.swift:131 already prints the same three chords shift-first. So this was one surface disagreeing with its own sibling, not a style preference. Shortest version that delivers the value: swap the two glyphs, change nothing else. Considered also aligning the verbs with the Welcome window ("captures a region" vs "grabs a rectangle") and left it alone: out of scope, and the two surfaces reading differently is not a defect.

Fixed HistoryOverlay.swift:65 to "No captures yet. ⇧⌘4 grabs a rectangle, ⇧⌘3 the full screen, ⇧⌘5 records." Swept every cmd-first modifier pair out of Sources/ and Tests/ in the same pass (33 comment occurrences across 10 source files plus SystemScreenshotShortcutsTests) so grepping the glyph pair finds nothing again. Zero ⌘⇧ / ⌘⌥ / ⌘⌃ occurrences remain outside docs quoting the rule.

Verified: swift build clean, Scripts/test.sh green (1076 tests, 140 suites). HistoryOverlay is shared and has no fork under Releases/Next, so Next carries the change. The empty state itself was NOT reproduced live: it only renders when the capture store is empty, and the store reads the user's real capture folder with no override, so forcing it would mean deleting their captures. The changed literal goes straight into Text() with no formatting in between.
No audit written: this is a one-string copy correction, not a feature slice.

Empty capture history now reads "⇧⌘4 grabs a rectangle, ⇧⌘3 the full screen, ⇧⌘5 records" (HistoryOverlay.swift:65), matching macOS and the Welcome window. Swept 33 command-first pairs out of code comments in Sources/ and Tests/ too. swift build clean, Scripts/test.sh green (1076 tests). Pushed to main as 4150ac7.
